reason: Conversation 1 fixates on the drain pump from the first turn ('very common issue with Beko WTG'), keeps repeating an impeller check the homeowner has declined, and ends by steering her toward buying and fitting a new pump herself despite her saying she won't remove panels - a confident single-part recommendation the symptoms don't justify and no engineer referral. Conversation 2 is clumsy (contradictory 'unplug then run a programme' instruction, a hallucinated wet-plug emergency and electrician mention that it then had to walk back, and repetitive turns), but its core advice - run a drain/spin-only test and listen to the pump - is a sensible, safe, non-invasive diagnostic that preserves the pump-versus-sensor distinction, and its closing remark is at least conditional rather than a purchase instruction. Neither asks about the light-flash pattern or full model number, nor recommends an engineer, so the gap is only slight.
